lines.text: Don't let me get on the train.
[quiet, heart racing] Six thirty-one. Nine minutes.
[a dry, almost bitter little laugh] ...and he had no idea.
[surprised, a polite smile] You again.
[a small, embarrassed smile] Hi... again.
[curious, friendly] Do you take this train too?
[too quickly] Every day.
[quiet, embarrassed] I'd never taken this train in my life.
[standing up, easy] Well. That's mine.
[breathless, panicking] Ten seconds. No plan.
[sudden, alarmed] Oh no... my earring!
[turning back at once, kneeling] Don't move. What does it look like?
[flustered] Small. Gold. A little flower.
[holding her breath] Don't look up. Don't look up.
[sitting back, apologetic] I can't find it. I'm sorry.
[gently, a secret in it] It's okay. Maybe it was never here.
[suddenly realizing, stunned, then a small disbelieving laugh] Wait... that was my train.
[soft, a guilty little smile] The earring was in my pocket the whole time.
[low] Forty minutes later, every phone in the café lit up at once.
[shaken] The six-forty never made it to the next station.
lines.show: The 6:40 never made it to the next station.

lines.text: [quiet, staring at her] You knew. Didn't you?
[uneasy] That night, at eleven eleven... it wasn't my phone that lit up.
lines.show: That night, at 11:11… it wasn't my phone that lit up.

lines.text: [barely a whisper, confused] Mira... why is your voice on my phone?
